newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian lower house approves anti-landmine law.
newsitem.headline: Italian lower house approves anti-landmine law.

text.p: Italy's lower house of parliament on Thursday approved a bill aimed at introducing a blanket ban on the production, sale and use of anti-personnel landmines, a parliamentary official said.

Italy has been singled out in the past by the United Nations as a major producer of many of the 120 million landmines planted worldwide, but is now at the forefront of moves to end to trade in the cheap, deadly weapons.

The foreign committee in the lower house of parliament on Thursday rubber-stamped the bill, which will ban not only anti-personnel mines but also other devices which could be transformed into anti-personnel mines.
The legislation received broad cross-party support and now moves to the Senate (upper house) for final ratification.
"This law is one of the most advanced and rigorous of its type," the foreign commission said in a statement.
Some 95 countries, including Italy, have expressed their support for the first international landmine ban treaty, to be signed in Ottawa in December.
The countries have signed the Brussels Declaration, which will form the basis for negotiations in Oslo in September on the exact wording of the Ottawa treaty.

"Italy will be able to go to international events such as the Ottawa disarmament conference with its cards in order to seek, with authority, a global moratorium (on landmines)," said the lower house foreign committee vice-chairman, Vito Leccese.
